neighboringSourceContext.speaker: Jonathan Haidt
neighboringSourceContext.claimSummary: More flourishing is better other things equal, but a life's value is not exhausted by summing pleasurable or happy moments because narrative and meaning also matter.
neighboringSourceContext.reasonSummary: A life with substantially more happy moments can nevertheless be evaluated as an utter failure in its final narrative; people care about purpose and the story of the whole life.

inferenceSummary.premise: People's considered evaluation of lives depends on meaning and narrative as well as momentary experience.
inferenceSummary.inference: A metric that simply aggregates experiential moments can rank lives incorrectly.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: Well-being understood as summed experience is insufficient as a complete moral criterion.

sourceSpan.excerpt: said ceteris paribus more flourishing is better than less it's just a question of whether this is all there is is the is the experiences and we add up the experiences uh you know as i said in one of my replies to you um you know what the view you're taking is kind of like dan kahneman's early work on happiness where he thought that um you add up the total moments of happiness and whatever life has more more of those moments is the better one but he changed his mind and one of the reasons is because while our experience of suffering and flourishing is important there are other elements and a big part of it is the story we tell about ourselves our sense of meaning it isn't just the total number of moments and i always do this with my my students i ask them which life would you rather have one in which the total you know i draw graphs one in which the total amount of happy moments or pleasure is you know 50 more over life which is huge but you know in the last 10 or 20 years the story you have about your life is that you were an utter failure um and um so it's our sense of meaning our sense of narrative there's more to a happy life than moments of flourishing and this is why i don't think you could measure with with an fmri scan or any other tool you can't just measure the amount of happiness or pleasure add it up and say this life is better than that

neighboringSourceContext.speaker: Sam Harris
neighboringSourceContext.claimSummary: The distinction between experienced and remembered selves already broadens well-being beyond momentary pleasure to whole-life appraisal.
neighboringSourceContext.reasonSummary: Harris describes moment-by-moment sampling and contrasts it with people's retrospective judgments about happiness, actualization, and the future.

inferenceSummary.premise: People's well-being includes both lived moments and reflective assessment of their lives.
inferenceSummary.inference: A sufficiently broad well-being construct can include global narrative evaluation rather than only pleasure samples.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: The measurement objection does not yet show a value outside well-being.

sourceSpan.excerpt: actually that's a good point because i argued with danny kahneman about this over at dinner unfortunately this wasn't public this was just private argument but it was a very interesting conversation because i pressed him on on precisely this point the terminology he was using at that point was the experienced self and the remembered self yeah right and so the remember itself is this retrospective look so you when you when you if you were just going to sample someone's experience moment by moment and and you stick in your well-being detector and just see how happy they were that would be the experience self moment by moment but the remember itself is when you ask them you know how good is your life how happy are you how actualized are you you know what how do you feel about your future then you get these these broader answers that you know summarize the last year of their life or so right but i'm talking

neighboringSourceContext.speaker: Sam Harris
neighboringSourceContext.claimSummary: Meaning, connection, and life story can be included within the thing measured as well-being, even when attaining them reduces momentary pleasure.
neighboringSourceContext.reasonSummary: People do not seek the pleasure profile of successful heroin addicts; they willingly undergo ordeals for connection, meaning, and a good story, all of which affect the total value under the curve.

inferenceSummary.premise: Considered human flourishing includes meaning, connection, and narrative, not merely pleasure.
inferenceSummary.inference: A well-being measure can track those experienced and reflective goods and their trade-offs.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: Meaning complicates measurement but need not constitute an independent moral foundation.
